- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early forecast periods (e.g., 1–3 days ahead); adjust by smoothing toward recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts mid-term decline; apply downward bias of 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to lag in direction; align forecast with sentiment swing midpoint, not peak.
